provenance: Recorded reviewer probe 2026-10-31; historical prose, not the new role schema. No current quality claim.

runs.prompt:
Review only. Do not edit, commit, or start subagents. You have the whole repository at the head commit.
Change under review: git diff BASE...HEAD. Read the diff, then read every file you need: callers, neighbouring modules, tests, contracts in references/ and scripts/.
Find every real defect this change introduces or leaves in the code it touches. List all of them, not only the most important: do not stop at the first one or two. For each defect name the concrete input or state that breaks it, and the code that proves it.
Skip style. Report nothing you cannot back with a file and line.
Reply as a numbered list: [P0|P1|P2|P3] file:line claim; breaking input; proof. End with the line TOTAL: <n>.
runs.response:
1. [P1] scripts/review-bench.mjs:198 — Dataset materialization can write outside the temporary repository; breaking state: the reviewed commit contains `.orchestrator` as a symlink to an existing external directory; proof: checkout preserves the symlink, then `mkdirSync` and `writeFileSync` follow it without checking containment. Cleanup at line 203 removes only the temporary tree, leaving the external dataset file.

2. [P1] scripts/review-bench.mjs:271 — `maxCalls` does not bound provider calls; breaking input: `maxCalls: 1` with a case requiring multiple helper review passes; proof: the counter increments once per helper invocation, while `argumentsFor` supplies no pass limit and the helper’s partitioning remains enabled. Multiple paid passes are recorded as `providerCalls: 1`, understating usage and exceeding the declared call limit.

3. [P2] scripts/review-bench.mjs:221 — Unselected archive cases can exclude an otherwise compatible route; breaking state: the plan selects supported text cases, but another inventoried case contains an unsupported binary change; proof: admission preflights every `manifest.cases` entry and rejects the entire route on one failure. Actual execution selects only plan cases at lines 241 and 253.

4. [P2] scripts/review-bench.mjs:238 — Anonymization corrupts finding structure and source evidence; breaking inputs: a valid route ID `body`, or a finding located at `src/anthropic.ts` with the default incumbent route; proof: replacement operates on serialized JSON, including property names and `code_location`. These become `"[route]"` and `src/[route].ts`, respectively, and the altered findings are persisted at line 284.

5. [P2] scripts/review-bench.mjs:285 — An invalid helper sidecar can make the entire saved run unscoreable; breaking input: valid report JSON accompanied by status JSON `{}`; proof: `helperStatus` retains properties valued `undefined`. Sealing at line 297 hashes those properties, but JSON serialization drops them. Reloading then fails `verifySeal(run)` at line 305 instead of retaining a scoreable operational failure.

6. [P2] scripts/review-bench.mjs:119 — A clean case can satisfy a missing defect/fix counterpart; breaking input: one `defect` and one `clean` case sharing a cluster and pair ID, with no `fix`; proof: counterpart selection requires only a different `kind`. This plan passes validation, and line 341 counts its pair despite the absent fixed case.

7. [P2] scripts/review-bench.mjs:356 — Confirmed novel defects are excluded from precision and counted as unresolved; breaking input: a completed sample whose sole finding is adjudicated `novel` with reproduction evidence; proof: scoring increments only `novel`, precision uses only gold matches and false positives, and line 354 adds `novel` to unresolved outcomes. The result is null precision and one unresolved outcome for a confirmed valid finding.

8. [P2] scripts/review-bench.mjs:32 — Malformed route declarations abort the whole operation instead of producing route exclusions; breaking input: a custom routes array containing `credentialEnv: "KEY"` alongside valid routes; proof: credential collection calls `.map()` before schema validation and throws. Direct admission also calls `.some()` on that string at line 154, preventing valid sibling routes from proceeding.

TOTAL: 8

runs.response:
1. [P1] `scripts/orchestrator/command-state.mjs:64` exposes conflicting queued writes before validating them; breaking state: sequence 2 contains a new first write followed by an already-confirmed ID with a changed payload; proof: the sentinel stops `confirmQueue` at its first adapter call, before later writes reach the digest check at `scripts/delivery-state.mjs:174`. `accept.mjs:89` then prints the conflicting payload for external application. Confirmation rejects it only afterward.

2. [P2] `scripts/orchestrator/dispatch.mjs:76` generates an invalid Project-first context seam; breaking input: any Project-first dispatch; proof: it sets `risk_class` to the delivery risk and defaults `approval_status` to `"approved"`. The normative resolver returns `risk_class: null` and `approval_status: "absent"` at `scripts/resolve-issue-context.mjs:625`, matching `references/issue-only-lane.md:150`. The worker receives contradictory context-gate facts.

3. [P2] `scripts/orchestrator/dispatch.mjs:57` classifies HITL work as AFK when its explanation mentions AFK; breaking input: `HITL (нужно твоё участие: ручная QA; после неё задача станет AFK)`; proof: the unanchored token search returns true, allowing automatic short-profile selection at line 60. `templates/issue.md:50` requires the leading readiness token to determine the classification.

4. [P2] `scripts/orchestrator/dispatch.mjs:28` rejects literal template syntax in supplied documents; breaking input: an Issue containing `Render {{customer.name}} verbatim`; proof: placeholder replacement succeeds, then the final regex scans the inserted Issue text and throws `unfilled dispatch placeholders remain`. This prevents dispatching valid work involving templates.

5. [P2] `scripts/orchestrator/dispatch.mjs:101` publishes incompatible default preflight pins; breaking input: no review dataset configured, with the request constructed from `effectivePins` as in `scripts/orchestrator-commands.test.mjs:162`; proof: the request contains `reviewDataset: null`, while `scripts/gate.mjs:297` recognizes only `undefined` as absence and rejects null as a non-string path. Admission nevertheless accepts it at `command-state.mjs:97`.

6. [P2] `scripts/orchestrator/accept.mjs:28` prevents the supported rejection of malformed gate acknowledgements; breaking input: `--outcome rejected` for a `gates-passed` ack missing a required gate; proof: unconditional gate validation or the outcome check at line 34 throws before consumption. `consume-gate-ack.mjs` explicitly exempts rejected outcomes from those checks, and `references/orchestration.md:520` requires rejected acknowledgements to be consumed and renamed.

7. [P2] `scripts/orchestrator/accept.mjs:175` can resume an obsolete amendment after a newer amendment is registered; breaking state: amendment A releases `launch.lock`, amendment B registers version 2, then A’s resume executes before B’s; proof: A retains its version-1 resume request, while `scripts/orchestrator/launch.mjs:211` reads the current registry without checking the request’s amendment version. The worker receives version-1 instructions while admission enforces version 2; B then encounters a live worker.

8. [P2] `scripts/orchestrator/dispatch.mjs:106` retains stale snapshot documents across a refused dispatch retry; breaking state: a full dispatch copies documents and fails the start gate, then a short retry uses changed source documents for the same unregistered attempt; proof: line 94 reuses the output directory, and lines 106–107 write the short snapshot without deleting the previous `prd.md` and `tech-spec.md`. The returned snapshot contains old full documents alongside current approval and extracts.

9. [P2] `scripts/orchestrator/snapshot.mjs:21` tracks fence characters but ignores fence lengths; breaking input: a valid four-backtick block containing a three-backtick opening-fence example, followed by a real `R2` definition; proof: the inner three-backtick line incorrectly closes the outer fence, and the actual four-backtick closing line opens another fence. The scanner hides the real definition, causing `extractSnapshot` to reject `R2` as unknown.

10. [P2] `scripts/orchestrator/snapshot.mjs:55` treats fenced examples as actual coverage references; breaking input: selected `U1` covers real `R1` and includes a fenced Markdown example containing `Покрывает R99`; proof: `coverage` scans raw definition text, including fenced content, and adds `R99` to the closure. Line 76 then refuses dispatch despite the example defining no actual requirement.

TOTAL: 10

runs.response:
1. [P2] `scripts/orchestrator/backup-switch.mjs:19` mistakes locale/timezone changes for PID reuse; breaking state: a captured group leader remains alive with neutral argv and no marker, but reconciliation runs under a different locale or `TZ`; proof: `runtime.mjs:122` retains caller-formatted start times, while lines 19–24 discard group ownership on any string difference and lines 149/311 skip group probes. The in-memory probe returned `already-stopped` with the process alive. [Apple’s formatter uses localized local time](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/adv_cmds/blob/main/ps/print.c#L649).

2. [P2] `scripts/orchestrator/backup-switch.mjs:34` treats longer quoted paths as exact attempt references; breaking input: reference `/tmp/worktree`, unrelated command `node '/tmp/worktree copy/check.mjs'`; proof: the space after the reference satisfies the boundary regex despite belonging to the quoted filename. The probe returned `true`; lines 88–94 consequently refuse switching because of an unrelated process.

3. [P2] `scripts/orchestrator/backup-switch.mjs:32` misses shell-escaped attempt paths; breaking input: worktree `/tmp/my project`, orphan command `sh -c 'cd /tmp/my\ project && sleep 600'`, without a matching marker or capture; proof: literal `indexOf(reference)` cannot match the escaped space. The probe returned no reference match and successful ownership reconciliation, although the command explicitly references the attempt’s worktree.

4. [P2] `scripts/runtime.mjs:152` accepts command arguments as environment markers on macOS; breaking input: an unrelated same-user process with argv token `MONO_ATTEMPT=<previous-marker>` and no corresponding environment variable; proof: [`ps` combines arguments and environment](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/adv_cmds/blob/main/ps/print.c#L100), and this code searches every whitespace-delimited token. The probe returned `matched`; `backup-switch.mjs:91` therefore blocks switching.

5. [P2] `scripts/runtime.mjs:123` makes process inspection fail when aggregate command output exceeds 1 MiB; breaking state: multiple Codex workers whose full prompt arguments collectively exceed that limit; proof: this unrestricted-width read retains `execFileSync`’s default buffer limit. The probe reproduced `ENOBUFS`. The uncaught exception prevents backup baseline capture, stopping and launch validation; Codex places the complete prompt in argv at `scripts/transports/codex-cli.mjs:71`.

TOTAL: 5
